meta.instrument: script/m14/incoming-gate.ts (ONE whole-population run with --dump, index-assisted; the closure is not chunked)
meta.populationRule: THE ADMITTED SET IS THE GIT-TRACKED SET, NOT THE DISK: per-checkout `git ls-files -z` under `$PWD/.corpus`, the router's extension list {scss} from script/m14/language-extensions.ts (`.sass` is the `sass`/css lanes' — 67 corpus files this analyzer is never given), present in the working tree, <= 1 MiB, dedup by realpath.
meta.populationNote: ONE WHOLE-POPULATION RUN, NOT SAMPLES: the arm parsed 4,433 of 4,433 admitted with 0 parse failures and 0 degraded, so every bucket below is the population's. THE ARM IS INDEX-ASSISTED ON PURPOSE: `.scss` is in src/ast/parallel-indexer.ts PROJECT_INDEX_EXTENSIONS and incoming-gate.ts carries an SCSS_DECLARATION_SPEC, so production builds a project index for this language and the resolution scope here is per project. The 2 over-cap paths are carried BY NAME in the population artifact (sass-spec/benchmarks/large_empty.scss, consul/ui/packages/consul-ui/app/styles/base/icons/debug.scss); a disk walk would be a different population.
meta.metric: ambiguous counted by DECLARATIONS (distinct declarations), not distinct kinds; amb(kind) is a subset reported beside
meta.analyzerDigestsNote: sha256 of the analyzer the arm measured, first 16 hex characters.
meta.armCommand: BB_CORPUS_ROOT=$PWD/.corpus BB_DUMP_LIMIT=2000000 bun run script/m14/incoming-gate.ts scss scss 0 --dump --index
meta.supersedes: THIS ARM SUPERSEDES the 2026-10-23 run taken before the Lead's shared-filter exemption 0f313a05d: that run measured the analyzer through a filter that DELETED every `@mixin <name>`/`@function <name>` target, so its TABLE 1 read `calls 0` and `mixes_in 0` while the analyzer emitted both. The superseded artifact and the reason are preserved at validation/m14/measurements/scss/SUPERSEDED-pre-0f313a05d.md and scss-gate-whole-2026-10-23.SUPERSEDED-pre-0f313a05d.txt — a number whose meaning changed is superseded visibly, never edited.

rules.measurement: one whole-population run; TABLE 1 of the incoming gate; the eleven-term closure re-checked here before writing, per type
rules.population: the whole admitted set; no stride and no subsample
rules.closure: resolved + amb(decl) + unresolved + bindOK + bind? + bindFAIL + extOK + ext? + extFAIL + causeOK + causeFAIL = edges. amb(kind) and collRes are reported beside their parent buckets and NEVER added. unclassed ceiling is 0.
rules.direction: resolved/external are FLOORS (may not decrease). ambiguous/otherUnresolved/unclassed are CEILINGS (may not increase).
rules.bucketMapping: external = extOK + ext?; otherUnresolved = unresolved + extFAIL + bindOK + bind? + bindFAIL + causeOK + causeFAIL. The five gate buckets are a declared coarsening of the eleven terms; every row publishes the eleven terms in `closure`.

P1:inclusion-specifier-no-project-file.statement: a `part_of` row whose written Sass specifier answers to no admitted `.scss` file by the lane's own spelling arithmetic, AND carries no file claim; the included part is a dependency, a `.sass` file (the css lane's population) or absent.

falsifier.wouldFail: a row whose specifier DOES answer to an admitted `.scss` file by the candidate spelling arithmetic (then the claim guard owed the claim and the row would be a claim defect, not a wall).

M1:mixin-not-declared-in-this-file.statement: a `mixes_in` row whose `@mixin <name>` target is not declared by the file carrying the `@include`; the name is declared in another file or in a dependency the project does not carry.

falsifier.wouldFail: a `mixes_in` target whose mixin NAME is in declarationsByRepo[repo].mixins (the project's own index owes that resolution, so the row would be an index defect, not a wall).

E1:selector-not-declared-in-this-file.statement: an `extends` row whose selector target is not declared by the file carrying the `@extend`; the per-file analyzer publishes this file's selectors, so a target outside it is genuinely out of reach.

falsifier.wouldFail: an `extends` target declared as a rule in the SAME file (then the analyzer's own-file resolution owed it, and the row would be an instrument defect) — a nonzero count here refutes the class.

F1:file-scoped-target-not-declared.statement: a `<file>::<member>` target whose declaring file does not declare the member (the file may be admitted; a member that moved or a selector spelled differently).

falsifier.wouldFail: a file-scoped target whose member IS declared in the named file.

E1b:extend-target-declared-in-same-file-.class: DEFECT: same-file extend target left unresolved
E1b:extend-target-declared-in-same-file-.statement: DEFECT CLASS, NOT A WALL: the `@extend` target selector IS declared as a rule in the file carrying the directive, so the per-file analyzer owed the resolution and did not make it. Counted so the defect is a number rather than a sentence; this class is NOT read as a wall release.

falsifier.wouldFail: a row in THIS class: the same-file declaration check is the refutation, and it fires on the rows themselves — which is exactly why the class is declared as a defect rather than as a wall.

N1:bare-name-not-declared-in-this-file.statement: every other unresolved name: a bare class/member/selector name whose declaration is in another file, in a dependency, or absent.

falsifier.wouldFail: a bare name whose declaration IS in the same file at a rule position (instrument defect rather than a wall).

resolution_caveats: THE RESOLUTION SCOPE IS PER PROJECT, WHICH IS PRODUCTION'S SCOPE (index=yes). `parallel-indexer.resolveRelationships` fills `target_symbol_id` only from a project-scoped qualified-name exact match, or from a bare name whose count IN THAT PROJECT is exactly 1. A name that collides with a declaration in ANOTHER repository reads unresolved here and would not necessarily read so in a pooled scope, and this lane publishes the per-project numbers as the verdict's.

`collRes` IS A SUBSET OF `resolved` AND IS NEVER ADDED: a resolved edge whose target had MORE THAN ONE declaration in the project, so production's own-file tie-break chose the row. The fleet's own indexer measures 37,318 of 49,729 such picks as WRONG, so this lane's resolved column is a FLOOR on correct resolution, not a count of correct edges. The number is published per row so a reader can discount it.

`amb(kind)` IS A SUBSET OF `amb(decl)`: it counts distinct KINDS among the colliding declarations, while amb(decl) counts distinct DECLARATIONS. Two different questions about the same edges; only the by-declaration count is in the closure.

★ `mixes_in` IS PUBLISHED FOR EVERY CLEAN `include_statement` — including includes whose mixin this file does NOT declare — with the target in the lane's published spelling (`@mixin <name>`). Those rows are UNRESOLVED rather than absent: the mixin is declared in another file or in a dependency the project does not carry, and the cause census counts them as M1. THE NAMESPACED FORM `@include ns.mixin` IS A MEASURED WALL: the served build splits the node at the dot, so the mixin name is not a node this walk can read; the extended census counts those sites (`includeUnparsable`) and R2 (a grammar patch to accept a dotted callable path) is the named available remedy, NOT taken this round.

★ `part_of` IS A LABEL MOVE, NOT A NEW EDGE: the Sass file-inclusion form of `@import` (exactly one `string_value` named child, specifier not a stylesheet URL) was published as `imports` by the CSS delegate and is published as `part_of` now, with the mandatory `metadata.partRole: "library"`. Source, target, line and the delegate's `importProjectFile` claim are unchanged. `imports` therefore holds the stylesheet-loading forms only (`url(...)`, a media query, a `.css` specifier, a protocol URL, `sass:`), and the `@use`/`@forward` RELATIONSHIP EDGE is still a MEASURED GAP with its own proposal (validation/m14/proposals/scss-imports-use-forward.md) — it is not claimed here.

★ THE TWO RULED TYPES ARE `decorates` AND `renders`, each with its ladder walked and its measurement cited in script/m14/spec/scss-completeness.json's `excluded` entries and in validation/m14/verification/SCSS-EXTENDED-TYPES.md: R1 was measured over the served build's OWN node inventory (validation/m14/measurements/scss-grammar-nodes.json: 90 named types of 195 ids; the decorator/render stems match 0), R2 is unavailable because a patch would have to INVENT SYNTAX the language does not have, and R3 has no node type that carries either relation (the near miss is `!important`/`!global`/`!default` for decorates — modifiers that name no callable — and `content:`/pseudo-elements for renders — value generation, not component rendering).

★ THIS ARM MEASURED THE ANALYZER THROUGH A SHARED FILTER THAT WAS FIXED MID-CAMPAIGN, AND THE FIX IS PART OF THE NUMBER. `src/ast/pool-worker.ts` `filterNoiseRelationships` (rule added 2026-10-21) refused any target leaf containing whitespace as a code snippet, and this lane's published callable spelling is `@mixin <name>`/`@function <name>` — so every `calls` and `mixes_in` row was SILENTLY DELETED before the store. MEASURED on bootstrap: before the Lead's exemption `0f313a05d`, `mixes_in 0 / 327 emitted`, `calls 0 / 51`; after it, `mixes_in 327 (213 resolved)`, `calls 51 (51 resolved)`. ⇒ A FIX FOR ONE LANE'S SNIPPETS WAS EATING ANOTHER LANE'S EDGES, and the earlier arm is SUPERSEDED (see meta.supersedes) rather than edited.

★ 27 OF THE ARM'S 553 UNRESOLVED ROWS ARE A DECLARED DEFECT, NOT A WALL-RELEASE: class E1b — an `@extends` target that IS declared as a rule in the same file yet left unresolved. The cause census separates it from the 128 E1 rows where the selector is genuinely out of the per-file analyzer's reach. It is counted so the defect is a number rather than a sentence; it is not released as a wall.

THE LANE'S `contains` EDGES CARRY A LARGE `collRes` SHARE BY CONSTRUCTION (a member answers to its owner's name, and CSS selectors repeat across files); the per-row collRes column is where a reader must look before comparing this lane's resolved share with a lane whose scope differs.
